subject: Feature bucketing & pilot seat uplift for TelcoWave
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@telcowave.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@telcowave.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Feature bucketing and pilot lift for TelcoWave

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput and routing controls look promising. Procurement asked me to follow up with the exact packaging we discussed: we want to run a 3-month pilot across two markets (East / West) with ~120 concurrent seats for the CX assistants and a second smaller bucket (~30 seats) for the backend QA team.

Two asks from our side:
- Can you confirm a simple bucket model (Core / Extended / QA) and whether we can move seats between buckets mid-pilot without penalties?
- What discount schedule should we expect for a pilot that might convert to a 24-month committed Dedicated plan?

I've attached our internal requirements CSV for reference. Procurement will need approximate ARR and unit pricing to start an internal approval.

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Digital Experience
TelcoWave

Attachment: TelcoWave_requirements.csv (CSV, 34KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@telcowave.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@telcowave.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Feature bucketing and pilot lift for TelcoWave

Hi Alex — great to hear from you, and glad the demo resonated.

Short answers up front: yes, we can support a 3-bucket pilot (Core / Extended / QA) and we allow seat reallocation within the pilot window: moving seats between buckets is permitted without penalty so long as total committed seats remain the same during the monthly billing cycle.

I've attached our current pricing matrix (v3) and a suggested packaging layout tailored to your 120+30 split. High level:
- Core bucket: base generation, low latency SLOs, token limits tuned for CX use.
- Extended: includes function calling & higher context windows for supervisors and escalation workflows.
- QA: low-cost batch evaluation capacity, lower SLO, lower priority for bursts.

For pilot-to-commit discounts, we typically offer a staged discount ladder: 10% for an initial 6–12 month commit, 18% for 12–18 months, 25%+ for 24+ months depending on GPU capacity reservation and ARR. Priyom (cc'd) can map these to hourly capacity and token economics. Rishi, could you flag any constraints on the discount bands for telco verticals?

Next steps I recommend:
1) We send a one-page Mutual Action Plan (MAP) outlining seats, buckets, milestones, and PO cadence.
2) Procurement provides a PO placeholder so we can reserve capacity.
3) We draft a simple SOW for the 3-month pilot (scope + success criteria).

I'll follow up internally and send the MAP by Monday.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood_pricing_matrix_v3.pdf (PDF, 78KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Feature bucketing and pilot lift for TelcoWave -- pricing ask

Rishi/Priyom — forwarding Alex's requirements. High level ask: 3-month pilot, 120 seats (CX agents) + 30 QA; possibility to convert to 24-month dedicated reservation across two regions. Procurement will need ARR and discount guidance.

A few specific questions:
- Rishi: what's the lowest practical discount we can offer for an initial 3-month pilot that preserves conversion flexibility? Can we do a pilot credit (one-time) + commit discount ladder rather than a multi-month rebate?
- Priyom: what configuration (quantization / model family / instance type) do you recommend to hit their latency SLOs for CX and keep unit cost reasonable? If there's a recommended plan name or SKU we can include in the MAP that will help procurement.

Link to the draft pricing sheet: https://app.redwood.com/internal/pricing/redwood_pricing_matrix_v3 (internal).

Ping me back with the conservative and aggressive options — I'll share both with Alex.

Thanks,
Soojin

(Internal note: keep telco discounts slightly tighter due to support profile + multi-region burst capacity.)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Feature bucketing and pilot lift for TelcoWave -- pricing ask

Soojin — quick reply with recommended bands:

Conservative (low risk)
- Pilot: no ongoing discount; provide $25k one-time credit applied to pilot invoice to defray setup and reservation friction.
- Commit: 12-month reserved capacity -> 15% off list; 24-month -> 22% off list.

Aggressive (convert-focused)
- Pilot: offer 10% pilot discount on usage plus $20k credit if they sign LOI within pilot window.
- Commit: 24-month reserved capacity -> 28% off list with a 10% upfront prepay.

Constraints/notes:
- For telco customers we need to account for multi-region burst capacity. If they require hard SLAs for burst volume, that increases committed cost by ~8–12% due to excess capacity reservation.
- Any discount exceeding 25% should be escalated to Sales Director approval and may require a support fee.

Attachment: dedicated_capacity_sla_excerpt.pdf (PDF, 22KB)

Priyom — what's your recommended instance profile and expected per-seat token cost for the CX bucket (95th percentile latencies <150ms for short-turn requests)?

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@telcowave.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@telcowave.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 15:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Feature bucketing and pilot lift for TelcoWave

Alex — thanks for the patience. Summary and proposed approach below (putting the conservative / aggressive options side-by-side so procurement can choose):

Plan summary (pilot):
- Term: 3-month pilot (East + West markets).
- Seats: Core (120 concurrent), QA (30 concurrent).
- Buckets: Core / Extended / QA — seats movable across buckets during pilot month windows as long as total committed seats are stable.
- Pricing: conservative route: $25k one-time pilot credit + pay-as-you-go; aggressive route: 10% pilot usage discount + $20k credit if LOI signed mid-pilot.
- Conversion to reserved: 12-month commit -> 15% off; 24-month -> 22–28% off depending on upfront prepay and SLA guarantees.
- Caveat: strict burst SLA for multi-region replication adds ~8–12% capacity premium.

Requested next steps:
1) If you want the conservative option, procurement can issue a PO for pilot start; we'll apply the one-time credit.
2) If you prefer the aggressive path, let's add an LOI milestone to the MAP with expected signature date and we will reserve a small burst buffer on our side.
3) I'll send a short MAP + SOW and the DocuSign envelope for the PO placeholder later today.

Attaching the MAP spreadsheet we discussed and a simple seat mapping worksheet. If procurement needs a formal cost table line-by-line I can export an ARR mock for the three options by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: TelcoWave_MAPlist.xlsx (XLSX, 42KB)
